evidence: Paths relative to .qc-cache/hireops-workspace-2026-10-03-r3/task. No criterion lists several requirements and then explicitly waives most of them. The optional clauses I found each allow a conforming alternative or exclude a sibling's outcome, and none lowers the bar: render gate 'a refusal message is welcome but not required'; 'hiding it is optional' in hro_move_one_stage, hro_reject_hired and hro_mgr_other_job; 'Whether the Observer's screens show such controls is the app's choice' in hro_observer_readonly, also backed by functional/prompt.md:23; hro_refused_put_back 'A UI that refuses before the card moves ... also passes'; hro_candidate_private 'refused or answered with only that candidate's own data'; hro_candidate_linked carve-out; hro_pol_live_thread 'This row owns the draft and focus; where the view goes while reading earlier messages is graded in Functional'; hro_pol_session_resume 'unless the sign-in prompt has already appeared on its own (that also passes)'. Whole-flow conjunctive bars such as hro_activity and hro_candidate_private are the skill's known false positive and are not flagged. The 5 visual likert rows each have one anchored scale. Not every criterion has one target, though. Each criterion is written as a success statement followed by a 'Fails if ...' list. In several criteria that list names fewer conditions than the success statement requires, so the judge gets a strict bar from the success statement and a looser one from the list. The task prompts no longer carry the template's resolving rule. The template has 'Pass only if all legs hold.' and its prompt says 'A criterion is a conjunction: every numbered leg must hold'; neither functional/prompt.md nor polish/prompt.md says this. hro_msg_compose shows the safe form: 'Fails if any of these differs.' Every instance: (1) functional/judge.toml:47 hro_add_email_rules: the success statement requires 'the typed name stays' (public: hireops_rules.md:34 'keep what was typed'). The Fails list (duplicate or invalid address saved / explanation not tied to email / other-job refused) leaves out losing the typed name. (2) polish/judge.toml:76 hro_pol_live_board, weight 3: requires 'typing more appends to it'. Fails covers only 'closes the details, clears or changes the note, moves focus or resets scroll', not the caret moving (public: instruction.md:7 'never touch my draft or my cursor'). (3) polish/judge.toml:85 hro_pol_live_thread, weight 3: requires 'typing more appends to it'. Fails covers only 'draft or focus is lost or the view moves'. (4) polish/judge.toml:103 hro_pol_failed_send: requires 'Remove the interception and send again: it is sent once'. Fails names 'sent twice' but not a retry that never sends. (5) functional/judge.toml:380 hro_candidate_view: requires job title and team on each application (hireops_rules.md:179). Fails names only 'wording, ownership or the conversation'. (6) functional/judge.toml:263 hro_activity: requires each line 'naming who and the stages'. Fails names 'no line, unattributed, out of order, or the filter drops or mixes lines'. A line that names the person but no stages is listed in neither (hireops_rules.md:111 'who did it and what changed'). Weaker: (7) functional/judge.toml:128 hro_undo_full: the success statement says 'refused and nothing changes', but Fails covers only 'Interview goes over its places'. I treat the success statement as the primary bar, because the wording is 'Fails if', not 'Fails only if', so many judges will apply it. A judge that reads the Fails list as complete will still pass the weak apps described in counterexample. That gives two targets, which is exactly what row 33 describes. No runtime run was needed for this static row, and no judge-run evidence was consulted; whether a configured judge actually splits on these cases is NOT EXERCISED.
counterexample: Weak app: (a) when an email is refused, it shows the error at the email field and clears the name input; (b) after a live board or thread update it keeps focus and the text but puts the caret at position 0, so further typing goes in front of the draft. A judge that reads hro_add_email_rules' Fails list ('duplicate or invalid address is saved, the explanation is not tied to the email, or a valid other-job application is refused') as complete gives 1. A judge that reads hro_pol_live_board/hro_pol_live_thread Fails ('clears or changes the note, moves focus' / 'draft or focus is lost') as complete gives 1 to those rows too, weight 3 each. Both apps break public requirements (hireops_rules.md:34; instruction.md:7) that the success statements require. A conforming app is not at risk, because the stricter reading only fails nonconforming apps.
suggested_fix: Give each criterion one target. Either end every success-plus-Fails criterion with 'Fails if any stated condition does not hold' (as hro_msg_compose does), or add the missing conditions to the Fails lists: typed name lost (hro_add_email_rules); typed text not appended at the end (hro_pol_live_board, hro_pol_live_thread); retry not sent (hro_pol_failed_send); title or team missing (hro_candidate_view); stages missing from a line (hro_activity); anything changed (hro_undo_full).
